question: On 22 August 2023, Elche City Council – led by the parties PP and Vox – removed two cycle lanes. It plans to replace more with ‘cycling streets’, where they would share road space with motorists. In its response of 13 December 2023 to a parliamentary question submitted on 5 October 2023, the Commission advocated cycling as ‘one of the most sustainable [...]

forms of transport and recreation’ and called for ‘more and better cycling infrastructure’. The removal of cycle lanes flies in the face of the European Declaration on Cycling of 4 October 2023, which highlights safety as a prerequisite to encourage people to cycle. The practice is also at odds with the provisions of Chapter V on the creation of more and better quality cycling infrastructure.

This decision is detrimental to the Zero Pollution Action Plan, the European Green Deal, the Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy and the new EU Urban Mobility Framework. Does the Commission consider that removing these cycle lanes in Elche is appropriate in light of the European Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan (SUMP)?
answer: The Commission proposal for EU Cycling Declaration (1) advocates for increasing safety levels for cyclists and other vulnerable road users, in particular by physical separation of cycle paths from motorised traffic where relevant, or by ensuring safe speeds in mixed traffic.

The revised Regulation for the development of the trans-European transport network (TEN-T Regulation ) (2) that is expected to be adopted by May 2024, after the political agreement reached by the co-legislators in December 2023, sets an obligation for Member States to ensure by 31 December 2027 the adoption and monitoring of a sustainable urban mobility plan (SUMP) for each urban node.

The regulation further prescribes that, when adopting and monitoring the SUMPs, local authorities, in cooperation with national authorities where relevant, shall make all possible efforts to ensure that SUMPs are in line with specific guidelines for the development of SUMPs (Annex V of the TEN-T Regulation).

However, the choice of implementing measures and their design is the prerogative of the Member States, and/or in some cases regional or municipal authorities, in line with the principle of subsidiarity which aims at ensuring that decisions are taken as closely as possible to the citizen.
